Read `README.md` and current rollout evidence first. Produce exactly one multi-wake target-policy candidate in `solver/`. Keep candidate-specific reasoning in `logs/optimize/wake_policy_notes.md`, and add or materially revise at least one evidence-backed reusable lesson in `guidance/control_experience.md` from the assigned parent, sampled solver results, and inherited logs. If no positive lesson survives the evidence, record a concrete negative result and what later workers should avoid or test. The candidate is incomplete until both files are updated. Work only inside this Phase 2 workspace.

This is the no-Bookshelf ablation: no cross-domain fish-control research shelf
is provided. Base controller proposals only on the task contract, current and
inherited guidance, sampled solver results, inherited optimizer logs, and
current rollout evidence. Do not search for or reconstruct the omitted shelf
from neighboring configurations or repository history.

I’m using the `read-wake-visual-signals-first` skill because this task changes a multi-wake dogfish target policy. I’ll first read `README.md`, the full skill instructions, and the current rollout evidence before inspecting inherited guidance or proposing the single candidate.

The contract confirms that visual evidence must precede any policy edit, and that the candidate must remain materializable throughout. I’m now locating the complete sampled evidence set and reading the remainder of the rendered task contract; I have not changed any files.

The scalar evidence shows a narrow family of failures: all four candidates exit left after roughly 66–74 release-time units, despite reaching 6.57–6.71 L from the target at best. I’m applying the skill’s visual sequence now—shared prewarm first, then the best-scoring rollout and the most diagnostic low-scoring rollout—to determine whether this is primarily weak propulsion, wrong steering, or both.

The visual sheets agree across all four samples: the fish initially propels leftward from the upper-right release, but the trajectory bends upward before reaching the target corridor and terminates at the upper boundary. The best sample’s extra lifetime/progress comes with higher lateral force and moment, not a qualitatively better path. I’ll now compare the assigned parent guidance, inherited optimization notes, and the exact sampled policies to isolate the parameter change that produced this tightly clustered failure family.

The inherited step-13 result is a concrete negative: rearward-only overspeed damping reduced the anterior peak only slightly (about 254°/time to 250°/time), shortened upstream travel from 4.44 L to 3.71 L, worsened mean/final range to 9.94/10.01 L, and preserved the upper exit. The skill requires confirming that topology visually, which I’m doing before selecting the next structural test.

The evidence supports one controlled extrapolation: restore the best evaluated `-0.25` rearward-bearing architecture and change only its behind-target authority to `-0.50`. The `0 → -0.25` comparison modestly improved lifetime, upstream travel, and distance metrics, while every added rearward damping/guard mechanism damaged the approach and retained the same exit. I’m recording that diagnosis and falsification boundary in the required notes before touching the policy, as the skill mandates.

The single candidate is now implemented: the evaluated approach gait and guards are restored, with only the gated behind-target bearing fraction changed to `-0.50`. I’m now distilling the inherited overspeed failure and the four-way rearward-control comparison into reusable guidance; this is a negative/conditional lesson, not a claim that the unevaluated candidate improves CFD.

Both required provenance files are updated, so I’m invoking the mandated check-runner sequence now. I’ll run the semantic guidance check, lightweight Julia contract/schema check, and editable-boundary check separately; no CFD rollout will be run.

The first mandated check exposed a rendered-workspace defect rather than a guidance-content failure: `README.md` contains the same copied-parent marker twice, so the checker counts two parents even though both entries name the identical optimizer. I’m inspecting the checker and exact duplicate lines to make the smallest safe repair, then I’ll rerun it.

The semantic check now passes after removing the duplicated identical parent marker. The Julia check itself could not start because this runner image has no `julia` on `PATH` (exit 127); that is an environment issue, not a policy assertion failure. I’m checking the standard local Julia locations and will run the same contract test if a binary is available.

All mandated checks now pass: semantic guidance, Julia policy contract/schema (using the workspace’s available Julia binary), and solver editable-boundary validation. I’m doing one final audit to confirm the candidate differs from the best sampled controller only in the intended rearward-bearing step and that the durable guidance change is isolated and evidence-backed.

Completed exactly one multi-wake policy candidate.

- [Candidate policy](solver/cases/dogfish_2d_shape_policy/candidate_target_policy.jl:1): restores the strongest sampled controller and changes only `behind_bearing_fraction` from `-0.25` to `-0.50`.
- [Candidate reasoning](logs/optimize/wake_policy_notes.md:1) records the visual diagnosis, evidence, hypothesis, and falsification boundary.
- [Reusable guidance](guidance/control_experience.md:106) now captures the negative damping/guard results and bounded rearward-bearing lesson.
- Semantic guidance, Julia contract/schema, and solver-boundary checks all pass.
- Removed one duplicated identical parent marker from `README.md` so the mandated guidance checker could resolve the assigned parent.

No CFD rollout was run.
